newsitem.title: UK: REXAM OPTS FOR HALF YEARLY FIDS.
newsitem.headline: REXAM OPTS FOR HALF YEARLY FIDS.

text.p: Rexam Plc, the UK paper, packaging and building materials group, said on Monday it would pay the half yearly fixed dividend on its convertible preference shares as a foreign income dividend (FID) following tax changes in the last budget.
Rexam said it would also pay the first interim dividend on its ordinary share as a FID in the year ending December 31.
Both FIDs, which will allow the group to save three million stg, will be paid on September 30 to shareholders on the register on August 22.
Rexam said it would also pay a second interim dividend on November 5 to ordinary shareholders. The size of the payment will be announced along with half-year results on September 16.
The government announced in July changes to dividend tax rules which mean pension providers and companies can no longer reclaim tax credits on dividends.

The advantage to Rexam of paying dividends as FIDs is that any Advanced Corporation Tax paid for such dividends which cannot be offset against the group's UK mainstream corporation tax liability should be recoverable from the government.

"This action should not disadvantage the vast majority of shareholders and will produce cash savings of three million pounds for the company which will benefit all shareholders," Rexam said in a statement.
